When they are about right, add in some thyme for the perfume and color.Tip: Whenever you are using herbs like thyme or basil, it is always best to break the herbs at the point you want to use them, for when you break the herbs, it is at this point that the perfume and aroma is the strongest.Prepare a mirepoix of onions, celery, carrots and leek.
Saute the ingredients until the flavors emerge and add a dash of white wine and let the alcohol burn up.

Add in sufficient chicken stock until the vegetables are fully covered.Peel the shrimp shells and add in the shells and tails into the mirepoix mix and bring the mixture to a boil, after which let it simmer for about 15-20 minutes. Season the shrimps with pepper, salt and thyme (or tarragon). Set aside.Season some chicken thighs with sesame oil, soy sauce and chinese wine and let it marinate for at least an hour.

Heat up a pan with some oil and fry some diced garlic. Put in the chicken skin side down first and let it cook for at least 2 and a half minutes, depending on the thickness of the meat.Flip the chicken thighs over and cook for another 2 minutes or so.

Add in a lemon's worth of lemon juice. Once the chicken is cooked, set aside and let it rest for at least 5 mins.Strain the mirepoix mixture and add in a knob of butter and some flour to thicken the sauce.

Add some ginger also to give that taste of the orient.In another pan, melt a knob of butter and add in some more garlic and ginger. Once the butter is melted, fry the shrimp for about a min or so each side and remove from the heat.To plate, place the potato cubes first, followed by the chicken thigh and the shrimp right on top. Sauce the mirepoix mixture around the plate.The final plate should be both visually appealing and a nice and refreshingly light alternative to your usual surf and turf.

steps: Peel the shallot and slice crosswise into thin discs, about 3mm thick.

Bring the oil just below its smoking point you should see light whisps of smoke, but not much more than that.Ensure the surface of each scallop is as dry as possible to encourage browning.

Place the scallops in the pan, leaving plenty of space between each one. Dont touch them for 60 seconds theyre busy forming a golden crust and if you move them, you risk tearing it away. After 60 seconds, lift the edge of one of the scallops to check for brownness. If it is golden brown, flip it over and give it another 90 seconds. If not, let it sit for another 30 seconds. Cooked scallops can still be translucent in the middle, but cook them to a doneness youre comfortable with.

Remove the scallops from the pan and turn of the heat. Toss in the french beans and let them sizzle for about a minute, soaking up the great flavor the scallops have left behind.To plate, lay down a pile of beans and divide the scallops between two plates. steps: Preheat oven to 180 C (350 F) degrees. Butter a 21 cm (8,3 or 9 inch) round cake pan. Line with parchment, and butter.

Beat in chocolate and chopped dates.
Transfer batter to prepared pan, and smooth top.
Bake until a toothpick inserted into center of cake comes out clean, about 1 hour.
Let cool in pan on a wire rack for 30 minutes. Run a knife around edge of pan to loosen, and invert cake onto rack.
Remove parchment, turn cake right side up, and let cool completely. (Cake can be wrapped in plastic and stored at room temperature for up to 2 days.)
Bring butter, dark-brown sugar, water, and salt to a boil in a saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally. Boil 3 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Whisk in cream.
Add chocolate, and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in brandy.
Let cool until thickened, 15 to 20 minutes.
Place cake on stand and pour glaze over top, letting some drip down sides.
Garnish with halved dates.

title: All Time Favorite- Gulab Jamun

steps: Make the syrup in a pan by adding water, sugar, rose syrup, cardamom powder and saffron.

For the dumplings, in a mixing bowl,add in all dry ingredients i.e instant dry milk, salt, all purpose flour and baking soda.

Allow the dough to rest for 10-15 minutes by covering it with a damp cloth or kitchen towel. Make desired size balls, make sure they are smooth and do not have any creases. (You can use a little oil on your hands and make the ball and flatten it out and then roll it again to a ballthis will help smoothening out the cracks)
Test the oil by dropping a small piece of dough, if it sits at the bottom of the pan for a few seconds before coming to the surface, the oil is ready.
Carefully drop 3-4 dumplings in the oil and keep rotating them for an even color.
Once the dumplings are a dark golden brown, take them out into a paper towel.
Bring the syrup to another quick boil and drop in the dumplings.

Turn off the flame and cover the pan and let them soak in the syrup for at least 1 hour. The more you let them sit in the syrup, the better. ( They soak up the delicious syrup, fluff up and becomes very soft)
Serve these HOT !

title: Bubble-Top Brioches
description: If you want to add more lacto ovo vegetarian recipes to your collection, Bubble-Top Brioches might be a recipe you should try. One portion of this dish contains approximately 6g of protein, 13g of fat, and a total of 247 calories. This recipe serves 12 and costs 35 cents
steps: Combine 1/4 cup warm water and warm milk in bowl of heavy-duty mixer fitted with paddle attachment.
Sprinkle yeast over and stir to moisten evenly.
Let stand until yeast dissolves, stirring occasionally, about 8 minutes.
Add flour and salt to yeast mixture. Blend at medium-low speed until shaggy lumps form, scraping down sides of bowl occasionally, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add eggs, 1 at a time, beating until blended after each addition. Beat in sugar. Increase mixer speed to medium; beat until dough is smooth, about 3 minutes.Reduce speed to low.

Add butter, 1 tablespoon at a time, beating until blended after each addition, about 4 minutes (dough will be soft and silky). Increase speed to medium-high and beat until dough pulls away from sides of bowl and climbs paddle, 8 to 9 minutes.Lightly butter large bowl. Scrape dough into bowl. Cover bowl with plastic wrap.

Let dough rise in warm draft-free area until almost doubled in volume, about 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes.Gently deflate dough by lifting around edges, then letting dough fall back into bowl, turning bowl and repeating as needed. Cover bowl tightly with plastic wrap and chill, deflating dough in same way every 30 minutes until dough stops rising, about 2 hours. Chill overnight. (At this point, use the dough to make 12 brioches, or 6 brioches and 1 tart, or 2 tarts.)Butter 12 standard (1/3-cup) muffin cups. Divide dough into 12 equal pieces; cut each piece into thirds.
Roll each small piece between palms into ball.
Place 3 balls in each prepared cup (dough will fill cup).
Place muffin pan in warm draft-free area; lay sheet of waxed paper over.
Let dough rise until light and almost doubled (dough will rise 1/2 inch to 1 inch above top rim of muffin cups), 50 to 60 minutes.Position rack in center of oven and preheat to 400F.
Place muffin pan on rimmed baking sheet. Gently brush egg glaze over risen dough, being careful that glaze does not drip between dough and pan (which can prevent full expansion in oven).
Bake brioches until golden brown, covering with foil if browning too quickly, about 15-20 minutes, keep a close eye on them.
Transfer pan to rack. Cool 10 minutes.
Remove brioches from pan.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

steps: Preheat the oven to 374F.Generously grease and liberally flour a madeleine cookie tin.In a small bowl, combine the flour, baking Powder and salt.

Whisk together and set aside.In a medium bowl, Beat the sugar and eggs on medium/high speed until the volume triples in size. This may take several minutes and you should have a beautiful thick 'ribbon' of batter when you lift the beaters out of the bowl.Stir in the orange juice and orange zest.Beginning with the flour mixture, alternate adding to the egg/sugar batter with the melted butter.

Mix only until just combined. steps: Grab your softened butter and spread it out on a piece of waxed paper to about 8x16.Stick it in the fridge and let it get good and cold.While your butter is chilling, you'll grab a bowl and dissolve your yeast in the water. You'll then add in the milk, sugar, salt, extract, and egg.

Mix it up well and then add in your flour. Use your hands to make a nice dough.Stick your dough in the fridge and let that chill down as well.When everything is good and chilled, pull it out and roll your dough out to about an 8x12 rectangle.

Cut your sheet of butter in have and lay one piece of it over 2/3 of your dough.Fold the third of dough without the butter over on top of the butter layer and then fold the other end over the top of that.Now chill it again. I recommend chilling over night and starting back up the next morning.For the next step, you'll grab your folded dough and gently roll it to an 8x12 rectangle again. Grab your remaining piece of chilled butter, lay it on the dough the same as before and fold like above.Now, you'll roll the dough carefully once more to an 8x16 rectangle and fold in thirds again.Stick in the fridge and take a break one more time.
Cut the dough in half width wise.Very carefully so as to not break any of the layers, roll the first half of your dough to a 6x20 inch size.
Mix up your filling ingredients.And spread it down the middle of your dough.
Sprinkle a few pecan on for good measure.Now close up one end, wet the edge with water and then close the other edge to create a seal.

Place your kringle on a parchment lined baking sheet and form it into an oval joining the two ends together. Flatten the whole thing down gently with your hands. Repeat this process with the second half of the dough as well.

Heat your oven up to 350 degrees and pop the kringle in for 20 to 25 minutes.While the kringle cools, grab up your glaze ingredients and mix them together well.Now head over to your cooled kringle and drizzle that beautiful glaze over the top of it.

Add onion to hot pan and saut until onions get slightly browned and caramelized for about 20 minutes.
Toss peppers in and cook for another 10 to 15 minutes.

While onions and peppers are cooking place steak on a roasting pan and broil in oven or grill for approximately 5 to 10 minutes per side. Be careful as this steak will be tough if cooked to well done. And it will continue to cook when removed from the heat so under cook it a little to account for this process.
Remove from heat and let rest before cutting.
In a food processor combine marscapone, horseradish, and squeeze out 4 of the roasted garlic cloves. (Store the rest of the bulb in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week)
Pulse a few times to blend.
Add next 6 ingredients and mix well.
Slice French Bread into inch rounds and heat in oven or on grill (grilled bread takes on a very unique sweet smoky flavor) until lightly toasted.
Cut steak into 1/8 to inch strips.
Smooth sauce over each warm piece of bread.
Top with steak and the onion pepper mixture.

steps: Hands on time: 15 minutes
Cooking time: 30 minutes or so

Serves 6Ingredients::4-5 dried shitake mushrooms6 cups water2 tbsp good olive oil4 large cloves garlic, minced (or finely chopped)1 large onion, diced1 tbsp fresh (or frozen) gingerroot, grated3 carrots, diced4 cups kale or collard greens, chopped2 cups cooked cannellini beans (I used 1(14oz/400ml) can of navy beans, drained)¼ cup mirin (I ran out so I used Chinese cooking wine)Healthy splash of tamari

Place the dried mushrooms in a medium pot with the water. Bring to a boil and then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes. When the mushrooms are soft, remove from cooking liquid and slice, discarding hard stems. Dice or slice and return to pot with broth.

Add the carrots and sauté for 3-4 minutes.
Add the kale, beans (I roughly mashed to thicken the broth), mirin and sauté until the greens are deep green and tender.

description: A wonderful tex-mex mint brownies - New England inspired and full of flavor.
steps: Combine the flax, applesauce and almond milk together in a small bowl. Set aside to allow to thicken. In a food processor, combine the blueberries, pear, black beans and oil. Pulse until the mixture become very smooth. Next, add the extracts and process until fully combined.
Remove the contents from processor into a medium sized mixing bowl.
Add the coconut sugar, cocoa, baking powder, soda, and salt and mix.
Add the flour with the chocolate chips and mix until just combined.
Pour the batter into your prepared dish and bake at 350 for 44-45 minutes.

Remove from the oven and allow to cool for at least 50 minutes. If you would like, place the brownies in the fridge for 20 or 30 minutes to speed up cooling time. While the brownies cool, start on your mint filling.In a small bowl, combine the soft avocado with full fat coconut milk or heavy cream. Beat on high for about 5 minutes until the mixture is fluffy and smooth.
Add the powdered xylitol and mix well.

Add peppermint extract and coloring if desired, and beat until all incorporated. Once the mixture is perfectly fluffy and creamy, add the flour and mix until just combined. The mixture should be thick and smooth but still easy to spread.
Spread the mixture evenly over the cooled brownies and place in the fridge for 10 minutes, until the mint filling has firmed.Next, melt the chocolate.
Add the oil to the melted chocolate and stir to combine.

Remove the brownies from the fridge and pour the melted chocolate over the brownies, gently and quickly spread the chocolate evenly over the brownies. The mint filling should be cold so the warm chocolate doesnt melt the mint filling, but the chocolate will cool quickly once it touches the cold mint. Make sure to work quickly so the chocolate layer will be even. Return the brownies to the fridge to cool for another 5 minutes until the chocolate is set.
Cut the brownies after the 5 minutes with a sharp knife.

Serve brownies chilled or at room temperature. Store any left overs in an airtight container in the refrigerator.NOTE: Once the chocolate layer has firmed, be sure to cut all the brownies immediately with a sharp knife. I cut some of the brownies when they were really, really cold, and they didnt cut clean and pretty.*For those who are not concerned with gluten content, wheat or white flour would work okay as well. For wheat, decrease the amount by 1 tablespoon. For the filling, be sure to use a white color flour to keep the mint filling a bright pretty green color.**You can use any kind of chocolate you like, but dark chocolate gives a wonderful flavor to the peppermint and sugar free dark chocolate is the easiest to find.

Transfer this back into the bowl with the rest of the pineapple and stir together check the flavour and add more honey or lime if you wish.Once your tapioca has chilled, place some of the pineapple mix in the bottom of your serving dishes, then add the tapioca and top with a little pineapple and some lime zest to finish.

description: Need a lacto ovo vegetarian dessert? Apple Cinnamon Cake could be a super recipe to try. One portion of this dish contains around 7g of protein, 28g of fat, and a total of 500 calories. This recipe serves 6. For 92 cents per serving, this recipe covers 10% o
steps: Sift all the dry ingredients together.In mixing bowl, cream butter and sugar till light and fluffy then add in whipping cream, continue to beat till light.Then add in vanilla flavor and eggs one at a time.Scrape bowl and add the flour ingredients, mix well.
Add in all chopped green apples and use a rubber spatula to fold well and pour into a 8"round lined cake tin.Lastly sprinkle the Crumble Topping on top of the apple mixture evenly.
Bake in preheated oven 180C and bake at about 50 mins.

title: Pumpkin Dessert With Butterscotch-Rum Sauce
description: Pumpkin Dessert With Butterscotch-Rum Sauce could be just the gluten free and lacto ovo vegetarian recipe you've been looking for. One serving contains 191 calories, 1g of protein, and 6g of fat. For 43 cents per serving, this recipe covers 7% of your daily
steps: For pumpkin dessert
Transfer cubed pumpkins into a large saucepan and pour the sugar all over.
Add two cloves to the saucepan (this step is optional)

Place the saucepan on low heat and close its lid.At the end of every 5 minutes shake the saucepan to blend pumpkins with melting sugar, if you prefer to use a wooden spoon be very gentle not to smash them.Cook until the pumpkins are tender then set aside to cool down.For butterscotch-rum sauce
Put the butter in a heavy bottomed stainless steel saucepan and melt it over medium heat.
Add brown sugar and stir with a spoon until the sugar looks like wet sand.
Combine the sugar beet/cane syrup and stir frequently till the caramelizing brown sugar looks more like a boiling viscous liquid (takes 4-5 minutes)

Add all the cream and lower heat, stir continuously with a whisk until they are well blended.Increase the heat to medium and cook until the liquid starts boiling while stirring frequently. This will take around 10 minutes. Keep the sauce on the heat for an additional 2 minutes after it starts boiling.

Remove from heat. When the sauce gets warm add rum, vanilla extract and salt, whisk well. Taste the sauce and add more salt or vanilla extract according to your preference.Fix pumpkin cubes on skewers and serve with a small bowl of butterscotch sauce and a few walnuts on the plate.

title: White chocolate-cranberry ice cream
description: If you want to add more gluten free and lacto ovo vegetarian recipes to your repertoire, White chocolate-cranberry ice cream might be a recipe you should try. One serving contains 429 calories, 7g of protein, and 28g of fat. This recipe serves 6 and costs $1.45 per servin
steps: In a medium saucepan boil the milk until it starts to bubble gently.
Remove from flame and set aside.Meanwhile whisk the egg yolks and sugar together for 3 minutes until pale yellow and double in volume.

Pour the milk on to the egg mixture and stir and then gently pour the mixture back in to the saucepan and simmer very lightly. Stir continuously until the custard mix thickens or coats the back of a wooden spoon.

Add the chopped chocolate stirring until the heat melts the chocolate.Cool the mixture, stir in the vanilla extract and put it in the fridge to chill.Once chilled, add the cream to the mixture. Stir and combine.
Pour the mixture into an ice cream machine and churn until frozen.
Add dried cranberries in the last 5 minutes of churning and let the machine stir them in.
Transfer to plastic container and place in the freezer for 3 hours before serving.

Bake for about 1 hour or until a toothpick, inserted into the center of the loaf comes out clean.-
Transfer to a wire rack to cool before slicing.

title: Chicken Enchilada Rice Casserole
description: Chicken Enchilada Rice Casserole might be a good recipe to expand your main course recipe box. For $1.2 per serving, this recipe covers 11% of your daily requirements of vitamins and minerals. One portion of this dish contains about 15g of protein, 6g of fat, and a total
steps: Preheat oven to 35
Bake chicken breasts in a baking pan for 30-35 minutes, or until juices run clear and chicken is cooked through.

Let cool in pan for 10 minutes before shredding using an electric mixer fitted with a paddle attachment or 2 forks.Meanwhile, cook the rice according to package directions or in a rice cooker with 4 cups of water and 1 tablespoon butter.Keep oven preheated at 35
In a large bowl, mix together the chicken, 2 cans of enchilada sauce, refried beans, and half of the cheese. Stir until evenly combined.
Add in the rice, seasonings, diced red pepper, and chopped green onions.
Mix well.
Transfer mixture into a large casserole dish. Top with the frozen corn and remaining cheese.
Bake for 35-40 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly.
Garnish with cilantro and serve warm.

title: Potato and Leek Soup – Potage Parmentier
description: Potato and Leek Soup – Potage Parmentier is a gluten free and lacto ovo vegetarian recipe with 4 servings. One serving contains 352 calories, 8g of protein, and 19g of fat. For $1.32 per serving, this recipe covers 18% of your daily requirements of vitamins
steps: In a large pan, heat 4 Tbsp butter until it bubbles.
Then add the chopped leeks. Season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Stir occasionally for about 10 minutes until the leeks get really soft and the edges begin to brown.
Add garlic and stir for another couple of minutes. Taste before the next step.
Add 5 c liquid (I use 50% chicken stock and 50% water) and the herbs. Taste and see if you like the balance so far. Some stocks are saltier than others.
Crank up the heat to bring it to a quick boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add 1 lb of thinly sliced Yukon gold potatoes and let it simmer with the lid on for about 40 minutes. Stir occasionally.

The soup is done when the potatoes are very tender and starting to fall apart. We might still have to add some more salt and pepper. Potatoes soak up some salt. Taste again. Season with salt until you achieve the desired yumminess. If you like, add a pinch of cayenne pepper, which really makes it pop.
Serve in a bowl, add a splash of heavy cream (if desired), and top with some fresh flat-leaf Italian parsley.
If you prefer a creamy consistency, use an immersion blender and blend everything together before serving.

title: Brown Rice Mushroom Pilaf
description: Brown Rice Mushroom Pilaf might be just the hor d'oeuvre you are searching for. One portion of this dish contains about 5g of protein, 5g of fat, and a total of 228 calories. This recipe serves 4. For 65 cents per serving, this recipe covers 11% of your daily requi
steps: Heat oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Saut chopped onion and sliced mushrooms for 5 minutes.
Add brown rice and stir to coat in oil.
Add water.
Bring to a boil, then simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove from heat and cover with a lid.
Let it rest until all liquid is absorbed.

title: No-Fail Caramel Custard
description: A wonderful no-fail caramel custard - Homestyle inspired and full of flavor.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees. Scald the milks together in a heavy saucepan.

Remove from the heat.Caramelize the sugar in a skillet over medium heat until it melts and turns brown. Slowly add the milks to the sugar, stirring constantly until the sugar dissolves.In a medium bowl, beat the egg substitute and egg yolk together until it is lemon-colored.
Add the milk mixture, port, and vanilla and stir well.
Pour the mixture into 6 custard cups and place them into a baking dish.
Pour boiling water into the baking dish so that the water comes halfway up the sides of the cups.
Place in the oven and bake until set, about 35 to 40 minutes.
Remove the custard cups from the oven and cool completely in the refrigerator. When they are chilled, place a dessert plate on top of each custard cup and invert.
Serve immediately.This recipe yields 6 servings.Serving size: 1/2 cup.

title: Crema Catalana with Orange Blossom and Toasted Almonds
description: A classic Spanish custard dessert with a crispy caramelized sugar crust, infused with cinnamon, lemon zest, and orange blossom water, topped with toasted almonds
steps: Toast the sliced almonds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until golden brown and fragrant, then set aside to cool completely.

Combine the whole milk, heavy cream, cinnamon stick, and lemon zest strips in a medium saucepan and heat over medium heat until the mixture just begins to simmer, about 8-10 minutes, then remove from heat and let steep for 10 minutes.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the egg yolks and granulated sugar vigorously for 2-3 minutes until the mixture becomes pale yellow and slightly thick, then whisk in the cornstarch until completely smooth with no lumps.

Remove the cinnamon stick and lemon zest strips from the milk mixture and discard them, then gradually pour the warm milk into the egg mixture in a steady stream while whisking constantly to prevent the eggs from curdling.

Pour the custard mixture back into the saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon in figure-eight motions for 8-12 minutes until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon and reaches 170°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Remove from heat and immediately stir in the vanilla extract and orange blossom water, mixing thoroughly for 30 seconds to incorporate the flavors evenly throughout the custard.

Divide the custard among six shallow ramekins or traditional terra cotta dishes, filling each about three-quarters full, then press plastic wrap directly onto the surface of each custard to prevent skin formation and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight until completely set and chilled.

Just before serving, remove plastic wrap and sprinkle 1 tablespoon of demerara sugar evenly over the surface of each custard, then use a kitchen torch held 2-3 inches away to caramelize the sugar in circular motions until it melts and turns deep amber, about 45-60 seconds per ramekin.

Sprinkle the toasted almonds over the caramelized tops and let the sugar crust harden for 2-3 minutes before serving immediately while the contrast between the cold custard and warm caramel is at its peak.
image_attribution: Photo by Cats Coming on Pexels

title: Thai Coconut Sticky Rice with Mango and Sesame Seeds
description: Sweet glutinous rice cooked in rich coconut milk with palm sugar, served alongside ripe mango slices and topped with toasted sesame seeds and crispy mung beans
steps: Rinse the glutinous rice in a fine-mesh strainer under cold running water for 2-3 minutes, swirling and agitating the grains until the water runs clear, then soak the rice in cold water for at least 3 hours or up to overnight at room temperature.

Drain the soaked glutinous rice thoroughly and transfer to a bamboo steamer basket lined with cheesecloth, spreading the rice in an even layer, then steam over boiling water for 25-30 minutes until the grains are translucent and tender when pressed between your fingers.

While the rice steams, combine 1 1/4 cups of coconut milk, the grated palm sugar, and 1/2 teaspoon of sea salt in a small saucepan with the tied pandan leaves, then heat over medium-low heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently until the palm sugar dissolves completely and the mixture is smooth.

Transfer the hot steamed rice to a large mixing bowl and immediately pour the warm coconut mixture over it, folding gently with a wooden spoon to coat every grain, then cover tightly with plastic wrap and let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes to allow the rice to absorb the liquid fully.

Toast the white sesame seeds and black sesame seeds together in a small dry skillet over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, shaking the pan frequently until fragrant and the white seeds turn light golden, then transfer to a small bowl.
In the same skillet, toast the split mung beans over medium heat for 4-5 minutes, stirring constantly until they turn golden brown and crispy, then remove from heat and let cool.

Prepare the coconut sauce by heating the remaining 1/2 cup of coconut milk with the granulated sugar and remaining 1/4 teaspoon of sea salt in a small saucepan over low heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then let it thicken slightly for 2 minutes without boiling.
Remove the pandan leaves from the sticky rice and discard them, then mound portions of the coconut sticky rice onto serving plates alongside the sliced mango pieces arranged in a fan pattern.

Drizzle the warm coconut sauce generously over the sticky rice, then sprinkle with the toasted sesame seed mixture and scatter the crispy mung beans on top, serving immediately while the rice is still warm and fragrant.
image_attribution: Photo by Likeboss lertpongsaporn on Pexels

title: Chè Đậu Xanh - Vietnamese Sweet Mung Bean Pudding with Tapioca Pearls
description: A traditional Vietnamese sweet soup featuring creamy mung bean pudding layered with chewy tapioca pearls, coconut milk, and pandan-infused syrup
steps: Rinse the dried split mung beans thoroughly in cold water three times, draining well between rinses, then soak them in 3 cups of water for 1 hour at room temperature to soften.

Drain the soaked mung beans and transfer them to a medium saucepan with 2 cups of fresh water, bringing to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are completely tender and beginning to break apart.

Mash the cooked mung beans with a potato masher or wooden spoon until you achieve a creamy, slightly chunky consistency, then stir in 1/2 cup of granulated sugar and the salt, mixing for 1-2 minutes until the sugar dissolves completely and the mixture is smooth.

Cut the pandan leaves into 2-inch pieces and tie them into knots, then bring the remaining 1 cup of water with the remaining 1/4 cup of granulated sugar and the tied pandan leaves to a boil in a small saucepan, reducing heat to low and simmering for 8-10 minutes until the syrup is fragrant and slightly reduced.

Bring 3 cups of water to a rolling boil in a separate medium pot, then add the small tapioca pearls in a steady stream while stirring constantly, cooking for 12-15 minutes until the pearls turn completely translucent with no white centers visible, stirring every 2-3 minutes to prevent sticking.
Drain the cooked tapioca pearls in a fine-mesh strainer and rinse them under cold running water for 30 seconds to stop the cooking and remove excess starch, then transfer to a bowl.
Heat the coconut milk in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 3-4 minutes until just warm, stirring occasionally, then remove from heat and stir in the vanilla extract, mixing thoroughly.
Remove the pandan leaves from the syrup and discard them, then assemble the dessert by spooning a generous layer of the mung bean pudding into the bottom of six serving glasses or bowls.

Add a layer of the tapioca pearls on top of the mung bean layer, then pour 3-4 tablespoons of the warm coconut milk over each serving, drizzle with the pandan syrup, and finish with a dollop of coconut cream and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds before serving warm or chilled.

title: Lavender Honey Financiers with Candied Pistachios
description: Delicate French almond cakes perfumed with lavender honey and topped with crunchy candied pistachios, featuring buttery brown edges and a tender crumb
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C) and generously butter 8 rectangular financier molds or a muffin tin, then dust with all-purpose flour and tap out excess to create a non-stick coating.

Place the unsalted butter in a small saucepan over medium heat and cook for 5-7 minutes, swirling occasionally, until it turns golden brown and smells nutty with dark amber specks forming at the bottom, then remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the almond flour, all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, dried culinary lavender, and salt until the lavender is evenly distributed throughout the dry mixture.
Add the egg whites to the dry ingredients and whisk vigorously for 1 minute until smooth and slightly thickened, then stir in the lavender honey and vanilla extract until completely incorporated.
Pour the browned butter through a fine-mesh strainer into the batter to remove any burnt solids, then fold gently with a spatula until the mixture is glossy and homogeneous with no streaks remaining.

Divide the batter evenly among the prepared molds, filling each about three-quarters full, and bake for 16-18 minutes until the edges are deeply golden brown and the centers spring back when lightly pressed.

While the financiers bake, prepare the candied pistachios by combining the shelled pistachios, granulated sugar, and water in a small skillet over medium heat, stirring constantly for 3-4 minutes until the sugar crystallizes and coats the nuts in a white, crunchy shell.

Remove the financiers from the oven and let cool in the molds for 3 minutes, then carefully unmold onto a wire rack and immediately top each with candied pistachios while still warm, pressing gently so they adhere to the surface.
image_attribution: Photo by Sena on Pexels

title: Spanakopita Rolls with Dill Lemon Sauce
description: Crispy phyllo pastry spirals filled with spinach, feta, and fresh herbs, served alongside a creamy dill and lemon yogurt sauce for a lighter take on traditional Greek pie
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat, add the fresh spinach in batches, and blanch for 45 seconds until wilted, then immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve the bright green color.

Drain the spinach thoroughly and squeeze firmly with your hands over the sink to remove as much liquid as possible, extracting at least 200ml of water, then chop finely and place in a large mixing bowl.

Finely chop the green onions including the green parts, mince the garlic cloves, and add them to the bowl with the spinach along with the crumbled feta cheese, ricotta cheese, fresh dill, and fresh parsley, mixing well to combine.

Beat the eggs in a small bowl, then pour them into the spinach mixture along with the nutmeg, black pepper, and half the salt, stirring vigorously until the filling is cohesive and the cheeses are evenly distributed throughout.

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper, then lay out one phyllo pastry sheet on a clean work surface and brush it generously with olive oil using a pastry brush.

Place a second phyllo sheet on top of the first, brush with olive oil again, then spoon one-sixth of the spinach filling along the bottom edge in a log shape about 2cm thick, leaving 3cm margins on the sides.

Fold the side edges inward over the filling, then roll the phyllo tightly from the bottom up like a cigar, creating a compact spiral roll, and place seam-side down on the prepared baking sheet, brushing the top with more olive oil.

Repeat the rolling process with the remaining phyllo pastry sheets and filling to create 6 rolls total, spacing them 5cm apart on the baking sheet, then bake for 26-28 minutes until the pastry is deeply golden brown and crispy.

While the spanakopita rolls bake, prepare the dill lemon sauce by whisking together the Greek yogurt, lemon juice, lemon zest, remaining fresh dill, remaining salt, and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a bowl until smooth and creamy.
Remove the rolls from the oven and let them rest for 5 minutes to allow the filling to set, then serve warm with the dill lemon sauce drizzled over the top or served alongside for dipping.
image_attribution: Photo by hamzaoui fatma on Pexels

title: Rosewater Semolina Cake with Orange Blossom Syrup
description: Moist Middle Eastern semolina cake soaked in fragrant orange blossom syrup and topped with toasted almonds, offering delicate floral notes and perfect sweetness
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a 20cm square baking pan with butter, then line the bottom with parchment paper for easy removal after baking.
Melt the unsalted butter in a small saucepan over low heat until completely liquid, then remove from heat and allow to cool to room temperature for about 5 minutes.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the fine semolina, all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt until thoroughly combined with no lumps remaining.

In a separate bowl, beat the eggs with a fork until the yolks and whites are fully blended, then add the plain yogurt, melted butter, rosewater, and vanilla extract, whisking until the mixture is smooth and homogeneous.

Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and fold gently with a rubber spatula for about 1 minute until just combined and no dry pockets of semolina remain visible, being careful not to overmix.
Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan, spreading it evenly to the corners with a spatula, then scatter the sliced almonds uniformly across the top surface.
Bake for 33-35 minutes until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean with just a few moist crumbs attached.
While the cake bakes, prepare the orange blossom syrup by combining the water and caster sugar in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely.

Bring the syrup to a boil, then reduce heat to medium and simmer for 8-10 minutes without stirring until it thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon, then remove from heat and stir in the orange blossom water and lemon juice.

As soon as the cake comes out of the oven, use a skewer to poke 20-25 holes evenly across the surface, then immediately pour the hot orange blossom syrup slowly over the cake, allowing it to absorb completely before serving warm or at room temperature.
image_attribution: Photo by Mohammad Fahim on Pexels

title: Butternut Squash and Black Bean Enchiladas with Chipotle Cream
description: Roasted butternut squash and black beans wrapped in corn tortillas, smothered in red enchilada sauce and topped with a smoky chipotle cream sauce and melted cheese.

ingredients.amount: 3 cups, peeled and diced into 1/2-inch cubes

steps: Preheat your oven to 425°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper. Toss the butternut squash cubes with 2 tablespoons olive oil, ground cumin, chili powder, 1 teaspoon salt, and black pepper until evenly coated.

Spread the seasoned butternut squash in a single layer on the prepared baking sheet and roast for 25-30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until the squash is tender and caramelized at the edges with golden-brown spots.

While the butternut squash roasts, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the red onion and sauté for 4-5 minutes until softened and translucent, then add the minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

In a large bowl, combine the roasted butternut squash, sautéed onion and garlic mixture, black beans, and 1/2 cup of the monterey jack cheese. Mix thoroughly and taste, adjusting seasoning with remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt if needed.

Reduce oven temperature to 375°F. Pour 1/2 cup of the red enchilada sauce into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish and spread evenly. Warm the corn tortillas in the microwave for 30 seconds wrapped in a damp paper towel to make them pliable, then fill each tortilla with about 1/2 cup of the butternut squash mixture, roll tightly, and place seam-side down in the baking dish.

Pour the remaining 1 1/2 cups red enchilada sauce over the rolled tortillas, ensuring they are completely covered. Sprinkle the remaining 1 1/2 cups monterey jack cheese evenly over the top and bake for 25-30 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly with golden spots.
While the enchiladas bake, prepare the chipotle cream by whisking together the sour cream, minced chipotle peppers in adobo, and lime juice in a small bowl until smooth and creamy.
Remove the enchiladas from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes. Drizzle the chipotle cream generously over the top, garnish with fresh cilantro, and serve immediately while hot and bubbly.
image_attribution: Photo by Rachel Claire on Pexels

title: Matcha Mochi Cake with Sweet Red Bean Swirl
description: A chewy, tender Japanese-inspired cake made with sweet rice flour and matcha green tea powder, marbled with sweet red bean paste and topped with toasted sesame seeds.
steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F and thoroughly grease a 9x9-inch square baking pan with butter, then line the bottom with parchment paper for easy removal after baking.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the sweet rice flour, granulated sugar, matcha powder, baking powder, and salt until the matcha is evenly distributed and no lumps remain, creating a uniform pale green color.

In a separate medium bowl, whisk together the whole milk, large eggs, melted unsalted butter, and vanilla extract until completely smooth and well combined, with the eggs fully incorporated into the liquid mixture.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and whisk vigorously for 1-2 minutes until you have a smooth, lump-free batter with a pourable consistency similar to pancake batter.

Pour the matcha batter into the prepared baking pan. Drop small spoonfuls of the sweet red bean paste randomly across the surface of the batter, using about 1 teaspoon per dollop for 8-10 dollops total.

Use a butter knife or wooden skewer to swirl the sweet red bean paste through the matcha batter in a figure-eight pattern, creating marbled streaks but being careful not to over-mix, leaving distinct red bean ribbons visible throughout.

Sprinkle the toasted white sesame seeds evenly over the top of the batter and bake for 50-55 minutes, until the edges pull away from the pan slightly and the center is set but still slightly jiggly when gently shaken.

Remove from the oven and let the matcha mochi cake cool completely in the pan for at least 1 hour, as it will firm up significantly as it cools. Cut into 9 squares and serve at room temperature, enjoying the chewy, sticky texture.
image_attribution: Photo by Gu Ko on Pexels

title: Honey Lavender Panna Cotta with Roasted Figs
description: Silky Italian cream custard infused with aromatic lavender and sweetened with honey, topped with caramelized roasted figs and crushed pistachios for a sophisticated Mediterranean dessert.
steps: Pour the cold water into a small bowl and sprinkle the unflavored gelatin evenly over the surface. Let it stand for 5 minutes without stirring, allowing the gelatin to bloom and absorb the water until it becomes thick and spongy.

In a medium saucepan, combine the heavy cream, whole milk, 1/3 cup honey, dried lavender buds, and salt. Heat over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the mixture reaches 180°F and begins to steam heavily but not boil, about 8-10 minutes.

Remove the cream mixture from heat and let it steep for 10 minutes to allow the lavender to infuse its floral flavor. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean bowl, pressing on the lavender buds to extract all the liquid, then discard the lavender.

Add the bloomed gelatin and vanilla extract to the warm cream mixture and whisk continuously for 2-3 minutes until the gelatin is completely dissolved and no granules remain visible when you run your finger along the whisk.

Divide the panna cotta mixture evenly among four 6-ounce ramekins or serving glasses, filling each about three-quarters full. Cover each with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or until fully set and jiggly when gently shaken.

Preheat your oven to 400°F. Arrange the fresh fig halves cut-side up on a small baking sheet. In a small saucepan, melt the unsalted butter with the brown sugar and remaining 2 tablespoons honey over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely, about 2 minutes.

Brush the honey-butter mixture generously over the cut surfaces of the figs and roast for 12-15 minutes until the figs are caramelized, softened, and their edges are slightly charred with dark golden spots.

Just before serving, top each chilled panna cotta with 4 roasted fig halves, drizzle with any remaining pan juices from the figs, and garnish with chopped pistachios and fresh lemon zest for a bright, aromatic finish.
image_attribution: Photo by Anat Landa on Pexels

title: Churro Cheesecake Bars with Cinnamon Dulce de Leche
description: Decadent cheesecake bars featuring a cinnamon-sugar churro crust, creamy filling, and homemade dulce de leche drizzle that captures the essence of Mexican street desserts.
steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a 9x13-inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving overhang on two sides for easy removal.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour, melted unsalted butter, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 2 tablespoons ground cinnamon, and salt, stirring until the mixture forms a crumbly dough that holds together when pressed.
Press the churro crust mixture firmly and evenly into the bottom of the prepared pan, then bake for 15 minutes until the edges are lightly golden and the crust is set.

While the crust bakes, prepare the filling by beating the softened cream cheese with the remaining 3/4 cup granulated sugar using an electric mixer on medium speed for 3-4 minutes until completely smooth and fluffy with no lumps remaining.
Add the large eggs one at a time to the cream cheese mixture, beating well after each addition, then mix in the vanilla extract until fully incorporated and the batter is silky.

Pour the cheesecake filling over the baked churro crust, spreading it evenly to the edges, then return the pan to the oven and bake for 35-40 minutes until the center is just set but still slightly jiggly when gently shaken.

For the dulce de leche topping, pour the sweetened condensed milk into a medium saucepan and cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon for 12-15 minutes until it turns a deep caramel color and thickens significantly.
Remove the dulce de leche from heat and whisk in the heavy cream, light brown sugar, and remaining 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon until smooth and pourable, creating a spiced caramel sauce.
Allow the cheesecake bars to cool completely at room temperature for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours or overnight until fully chilled and firm to the touch.

Using the parchment overhang, lift the entire cheesecake from the pan, cut into 12 equal bars with a sharp knife wiped clean between cuts, then drizzle generously with the cinnamon dulce de leche before serving.
image_attribution: Photo by Lam N on Pexels

title: Coconut Rum Cake with Lime Glaze and Toasted Coconut
description: A moist Caribbean-inspired bundt cake infused with dark rum and coconut milk, topped with a tangy lime glaze and crowned with golden toasted coconut flakes.
steps: Preheat your oven to 325°F (165°C) and thoroughly grease a 10-inch bundt pan with butter, then dust with flour, tapping out any excess to ensure the cake releases cleanly.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until evenly combined, then set aside.

Using a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, cream the softened unsalted butter and granulated sugar together on medium-high speed for 5-6 minutes until the mixture is pale yellow, fluffy, and increased in volume.
Add the large eggs one at a time to the butter mixture, beating for 30 seconds after each addition and scraping down the bowl sides as needed to ensure thorough incorporation.
In a liquid measuring cup, combine the coconut milk, dark rum, and vanilla extract, whisking gently to blend the liquids together.

With the mixer on low speed, alternate adding the flour mixture and the coconut milk mixture to the butter mixture in three additions, beginning and ending with the flour, mixing only until just combined after each addition to avoid overmixing.
Fold in the sweetened shredded coconut using a rubber spatula, ensuring it is evenly distributed throughout the batter without deflating the mixture.
Pour the batter into the prepared bundt pan, smoothing the top with the spatula, then tap the pan firmly on the counter 3-4 times to release any large air bubbles.
Bake for 50-55 minutes until a long wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out with just a few moist crumbs attached and the cake has pulled slightly away from the pan sides.

While the cake bakes, toast the unsweetened coconut flakes in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly until golden brown and fragrant, then immediately transfer to a plate to cool.
Let the baked cake cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then carefully invert onto a wire cooling rack and allow it to cool completely for at least 1 hour.
Prepare the lime glaze by whisking together the powdered sugar, fresh lime juice, and lime zest in a bowl until smooth and pourable, adjusting consistency with additional lime juice if needed.

Place the cooled cake on a serving platter and pour the lime glaze over the top, allowing it to drip down the sides naturally, then immediately sprinkle the toasted coconut flakes over the glazed surface before it sets.
image_attribution: Photo by cottonbro studio on Pexels

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding with Date Caramel Sauce
description: Classic British steamed pudding made with chopped dates and dark molasses, drenched in a rich toffee caramel sauce that creates an irresistibly moist and indulgent dessert.
steps: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and generously butter a 9x9-inch square baking dish, then set aside while you prepare the date mixture.

Place the chopped pitted dates in a heatproof bowl, pour the boiling water over them, then stir in the baking soda and let the mixture sit for 15 minutes until the dates are very soft and beginning to break down.

In a large mixing bowl, beat the 1/2 cup softened unsalted butter with 1 cup packed dark brown sugar using an electric mixer on medium speed for 4-5 minutes until light and fluffy with a mousse-like texture.
Add the large eggs one at a time to the butter mixture, beating well after each addition, then mix in the vanilla extract and blackstrap molasses until the batter is smooth and glossy.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking powder, salt, and ground ginger until the dry ingredients are thoroughly combined.
Add the flour mixture to the butter mixture in two additions, mixing on low speed just until combined and no dry streaks remain, being careful not to overmix.
Mash the soaked dates lightly with a fork to create a chunky puree, then fold this date mixture along with any remaining liquid into the batter using a rubber spatula until evenly distributed.

Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish, spreading it evenly to the corners, then bake for 40-45 minutes until the pudding is deeply golden brown on top and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.

While the pudding bakes, prepare the toffee sauce by combining the remaining 6 tablespoons unsalted butter, 1 1/2 cups packed dark brown sugar, heavy cream, and golden syrup in a medium saucepan over medium heat.

Bring the toffee sauce to a gentle boil, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the sauce has thickened enough to coat the back of the spoon and has a deep amber color.
Remove the pudding from the oven when done and immediately poke holes all over the surface using a wooden skewer, making approximately 20-25 holes that penetrate halfway through the cake.

Pour half of the hot toffee sauce evenly over the warm pudding, allowing it to soak into the holes for 10 minutes, then cut into 8 squares and serve each portion with additional warm toffee sauce drizzled generously over the top.

title: Cardamom Pistachio Shrikhand with Saffron Honey
description: A luxurious Indian dessert featuring strained yogurt whipped with cardamom, pistachio paste, and topped with saffron-infused honey. This creamy, aromatic sweet is traditionally served chilled and garnished with rose petals.
steps: Line a fine-mesh strainer with 3 layers of cheesecloth and place it over a large bowl. Pour the whole milk yogurt into the cheesecloth, gather the edges, and tie with kitchen twine. Refrigerate for 6-8 hours or overnight until the yogurt reduces to about 1.5 cups of thick, creamy consistency and whey has drained into the bowl below.

Remove seeds from the green cardamom pods by crushing them gently with the flat side of a knife, then grind the seeds using a mortar and pestle until you have a fine powder, yielding about 3/4 teaspoon of freshly ground cardamom.

In a small skillet over medium heat, melt the unsalted butter and add the raw pistachios. Toast for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until the pistachios become fragrant and lightly golden. Allow to cool for 5 minutes, then grind 1/2 cup of the toasted pistachios in a food processor with 1 tablespoon of powdered sugar until it forms a smooth paste, about 2 minutes. Roughly chop the remaining 1/4 cup pistachios and set aside for garnish.

In a small bowl, combine the saffron threads with the warm milk and let steep for 10 minutes until the milk turns deep golden yellow. In a separate small saucepan, gently warm the honey over low heat for 2 minutes, then stir in the saffron-infused milk and remove from heat immediately.

Transfer the strained yogurt to a large mixing bowl and whisk vigorously for 2 minutes until smooth and creamy. Add the remaining powdered sugar, ground cardamom, pistachio paste, and rose water. Using an electric mixer on medium speed, beat for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes light, fluffy, and completely homogeneous with no visible streaks.

Divide the shrikhand among 4 serving bowls or glasses, creating smooth, even portions. Drizzle each serving with 1 tablespoon of the saffron honey, then garnish with the reserved chopped pistachios and dried rose petals. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving to allow flavors to meld and the dessert to chill completely.

title: Coconut Tapioca Pearls with Mung Bean and Pandan
description: A vibrant Vietnamese dessert combining chewy tapioca pearls in sweet coconut milk, layered with smooth mung bean paste and fragrant pandan. This colorful che is served cold with crushed ice for a refreshing treat.
steps: Rinse the dried split mung beans thoroughly under cold water, then place them in a medium saucepan with 2 cups of water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mung beans are completely soft and can be easily mashed with a spoon. Most of the water should be absorbed.

While the mung beans are still hot, add 1/4 cup of granulated sugar and 1/8 teaspoon of salt. Mash vigorously with a potato masher or fork for 3-4 minutes until you achieve a smooth, thick paste. If the mixture is too dry, add 1-2 tablespoons of water. Set aside to cool to room temperature.

Bring a large pot with 3 cups of water to a rolling boil over high heat. Add the small tapioca pearls and stir immediately to prevent sticking. Boil for 12-15 minutes, stirring every 2-3 minutes, until the pearls become translucent with no white centers remaining. Drain in a colander and rinse under cold water for 1 minute, then set aside.

Cut the fresh pandan leaves into 2-inch pieces and blend them in a blender with 1/2 cup of water on high speed for 1 minute until completely pulverized. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing firmly to extract all the bright green pandan juice, yielding about 1/4 cup of concentrated liquid.

In a medium saucepan, combine the coconut milk, remaining 1/2 cup of granulated sugar, remaining 1/8 teaspoon of salt, and the pandan juice. Whisk the cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of cold water until smooth, then add to the coconut mixture. Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 5-7 minutes until the mixture thickens slightly and comes to a gentle simmer. Remove from heat and let cool for 15 minutes.

To assemble, place 2-3 tablespoons of the mung bean paste in the bottom of each serving glass or bowl. Add a layer of cooked tapioca pearls (about 3 tablespoons per serving), then pour the pandan coconut milk over the top until the glass is three-quarters full. Top each serving with 1/2 cup of crushed ice and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately while still cold.

title: Orange Blossom Semolina Cake with Walnut Syrup
description: A moist Middle Eastern semolina cake infused with orange blossom water and yogurt, soaked in a fragrant walnut-honey syrup. This basbousa-style dessert features a golden crust and tender crumb, garnished with caramelized walnuts.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Melt the unsalted butter in a small saucepan over low heat, then let it cool for 5 minutes. Grease an 8-inch square baking pan thoroughly with 1 tablespoon of the melted butter, ensuring all corners are coated.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the fine semolina, 1/2 cup of granulated sugar, and baking powder. Whisk together for 30 seconds to evenly distribute the ingredients. Add the plain yogurt, remaining melted butter, 2 tablespoons of orange blossom water, and vanilla extract. Stir with a wooden spoon for 2-3 minutes until you have a thick, smooth batter with no dry pockets of semolina visible.

Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and spread it evenly with a spatula, smoothing the top surface completely. Using a sharp knife, score the batter into diamond or square shapes, cutting about halfway through the depth. Place one walnut half in the center of each scored piece, pressing gently so the nuts adhere to the surface.

Bake in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes, until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. The edges should pull away slightly from the pan and the surface should feel firm to the touch. Remove from oven and let rest in the pan.

While the cake bakes, prepare the walnut syrup by combining the remaining 1/2 cup of granulated sugar, honey, water, and lemon juice in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the syrup thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon. Chop the remaining walnuts (about 1/2 cup) finely and add them to the syrup along with the remaining 1 tablespoon of orange blossom water. Simmer for 2 more minutes, then remove from heat.

Immediately after removing the cake from the oven while it is still hot, pour the warm walnut syrup evenly over the entire surface, allowing it to seep into the scored cuts. Use a spoon to ensure the syrup penetrates deeply into all the crevices. Let the cake absorb the syrup for at least 2 hours at room temperature before cutting along the scored lines and serving. The cake should be moist and completely saturated with the fragrant syrup.

title: Catalan Crema Catalana with Honey-Roasted Figs and Marcona Almonds
description: A luxurious Spanish custard dessert with a caramelized sugar crust, topped with honey-roasted fresh figs and crunchy Marcona almonds, infused with cinnamon and orange zest.
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and arrange the fresh figs cut-side up on a parchment-lined baking sheet, then drizzle the honey evenly over them and dot with the unsalted butter broken into small pieces.

Roast the figs in the preheated oven for 18-22 minutes until they are caramelized at the edges and their juices have begun to bubble and thicken, then remove from oven and set aside to cool while you prepare the custard.

In a medium saucepan, combine the whole milk, heavy cream, orange zest, and cinnamon stick, then heat over medium heat until the mixture reaches 180°F and tiny bubbles form around the edges, about 8-10 minutes, being careful not to boil.

While the milk mixture heats, whisk together the egg yolks, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, cornstarch, and vanilla extract in a large bowl until the mixture is pale yellow and smooth, about 2 minutes of vigorous whisking.

Remove the cinnamon stick from the hot milk mixture and slowly pour about 1 cup of the hot liquid into the egg yolk mixture while whisking constantly to temper the eggs, then pour the tempered egg mixture back into the saucepan while continuing to whisk.

Cook the custard over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon in figure-eight motions, until it thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon and reaches 175°F, about 6-8 minutes, ensuring it does not boil.

Strain the thickened custard through a fine-mesh sieve into four shallow ceramic ramekins or traditional cazuela dishes, filling each about three-quarters full, then refrigerate uncovered for at least 3 hours or until completely set and chilled.

Just before serving, sprinkle 1 tablespoon of the remaining granulated sugar evenly over the surface of each chilled custard, then use a kitchen torch to caramelize the sugar by moving the flame in circular motions until it turns deep amber and forms a crisp crust, about 45-60 seconds per ramekin.

Top each crema catalana with 4 honey-roasted fig halves arranged decoratively, scatter the roughly chopped Marcona almonds over the top, and serve immediately while the caramelized crust is still crackling and the custard is cold.

title: Sticky Toffee Pudding with Dates and Whisky Caramel Sauce
description: A classic British steamed sponge cake studded with chopped dates and drenched in a rich whisky-spiked toffee sauce, served warm with a cloud of lightly whipped cream.

ingredients.amount: 3/4 cup plus 1/2 cup for serving, divided

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease four individual 6-ounce ramekins thoroughly with butter, then place them on a rimmed baking sheet.

Place the chopped pitted dates in a heatproof bowl, pour the boiling water over them, then stir in the baking soda and let the mixture stand for 15 minutes until the dates have softened and the liquid has cooled to lukewarm.
In a medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt until evenly combined and set aside.

In a large mixing bowl, cream together 1/4 cup unsalted butter and 1/2 cup light brown sugar using an electric mixer on medium speed for 3-4 minutes until the mixture is light and fluffy, scraping down the sides of the bowl halfway through.
Add the large eggs one at a time to the butter mixture, beating well after each addition for about 30 seconds, then mix in the vanilla extract until fully incorporated.

Add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients and fold gently with a spatula until just combined with a few small lumps remaining, then fold in the date mixture along with all of its soaking liquid until the batter is uniform and slightly loose.

Divide the batter evenly among the prepared ramekins, filling each about two-thirds full, then bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes until the puddings are risen, golden brown on top, and a skewer inserted into the center comes out with just a few moist crumbs.

While the puddings bake, prepare the whisky caramel sauce by combining the remaining 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 3/4 cup light brown sugar, and 3/4 cup heavy cream in a medium saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves completely, about 3-4 minutes.

Bring the caramel sauce to a gentle boil and cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon and turns a rich amber color, then remove from heat and stir in the whisky.

Remove the puddings from the oven and let them cool in the ramekins for 5 minutes, then use a skewer to poke 8-10 holes in the top of each pudding and pour 2-3 tablespoons of the warm whisky caramel sauce over each one, allowing it to soak in.
Whip the remaining 1/2 cup heavy cream in a chilled bowl using an electric mixer on medium-high speed for 2-3 minutes until soft peaks form when the beaters are lifted.

Serve the sticky toffee puddings warm directly in their ramekins or carefully inverted onto serving plates, drizzled with additional whisky caramel sauce and topped with a generous dollop of the whipped cream.
